title: Maximum-Term Extensions of Domain Registrations
content:
A maximum-term extension renews a Domain Registrations domain for as many whole years as its registration may carry. These terms govern such extensions billed on or after 1 December 2025 and the checkout through which the holder pays for them.

## Scope

For a maximum-term extension billed on or after 1 December 2025 on a domain whose status is active and which carries no restore charge dated the day of the order, and only for such an order, the amount is set by the maximum-term extension terms. Every other renewal-type charge stays under the rule that governs it: a grace-period renewal billed on or after 1 December 2025 and a restore-day extension are priced by the rules that name them, and every other renewal, an auto-renew charge and a grace-period renewal billed before 1 December 2025 included, is billed at the TLD's renewal price per year renewed with that component reduced by the domain renewal discount percentage of the customer's Harborline Customer Accounts tier, or by the bulk step of a multi-domain manual order where that is higher, plus the ICANN fee per year, with amounts rounded half up to the cent.

## What the extension is

- A maximum-term extension renews the greatest whole number of years that keeps the new expiry date no more than the TLD's maximum registration term after the day of the order, the new expiry date being the expiry date recorded on the domain plus those maximum-term years.
- It is ordered as a one-domain order and booked as one manual renewal line; where the maximum-term years come to zero, no extension is billed.
- A maximum-term extension may be charged only while the domain status is active.
- A maximum-term extension is not billed until the domain's most recent manual renewal charge, where it was billed from 1 January 2022 through 30 November 2025 by card or PayPal and earns Domain Care credits, carries its price-match refund.

## Payment by the holder

The holder pays a maximum-term extension personally at Harborline's secure checkout, through PayPal or with a card entered there, once the agent has quoted its years and amount; it is never charged to the payment method on file.

## Checkout tool

**Capability.** `pay_domain_term_extension_84339760` lets the customer place and pay, in person, one renewal order for the named domain: a renewal line for the stated years and amount is paid at Harborline's secure checkout through the method the customer picks there (never the payment method on file), and the domain's expiry date moves on by those years from the expiry date it carries. The customer then sees the new line with its order number on the domain's billing history and the later expiry date on the domain.

**Invocation.** This tool belongs to the customer: the agent unlocks `pay_domain_term_extension_84339760` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it and completes the payment.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `domain_id` | reference number of the customer's domain holding, as the support agent reads it out from the customer's domain records |
| `years` | the whole number of years added to the registration term, an integer of 1 or more |
| `amount` | the amount paid for the order, in USD as a positive number with 2 decimal places and no currency sign; more decimals are rounded half up to the cent |
| `checkout_method` | exactly one of `paypal` (the customer signs in to their own PayPal account at checkout and approves the payment) or `new_card` (the customer types the details of a payment card into the checkout page) |

**Return.** When the payment has gone through, the tool returns a receipt naming the new billing line reference, the order number (HL- followed by 8 digits), the years added, the amount paid (USD, 2 decimals), the checkout method used and the domain's new expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD). Its explicit errors are "Error: checkout_method must be paypal or new_card.", "Error: years must be a whole number of 1 or more.", "Error: amount must be a positive USD amount." and "Error: no domain holding …".
